decisions.statement: The rungs are read off a scale page rather than named here.
A rung stated as text is read as the number that rung spells.
A figure given as text is read as the number that text spells.
A rung a scale states nothing for is no rung.
A climbing scale stating no black rung has its black rung read at zero.
The black rung read in is taken only where the rungs then climb.
The rungs are ordered from black through blue rather than by the numbers the rungs state.
A reading reaches the highest rung whose number the reading has gone over.
A reading under every rung is black.
The color a reading under every rung is given is named here rather than by a reader.
The tier above the tier reached is the next rung the scale states.
A rung the scale states nothing for is never named as the tier above.
The tier above a reading under every rung is the first rung that is not black.
How far a reading has climbed is the fraction between the rung reached and the rung above.
A reading under every rung has climbed a fraction that is unknown rather than zero.
A reading on the highest rung has no tier above that rung.
A scale of fewer than two rungs says nothing about which way a reading runs.
A scale whose numbers shrink from black through blue is read as a falling scale.
A scale whose rungs neither climb nor fall is refused.
A falling reading reaches the first rung from black whose number the reading has not gone under.
A reading under every rung of a falling scale is on the best rung that scale states.
A falling rung holds the band from that rung's number up to the number of the rung before.
How far a falling reading has come is the fraction of the rung's band the reading has come down.
A reading over every rung of a falling scale has come a fraction that is unknown rather than zero.
A reading that is no finite number reaches no rung.
A figure is floored rather than rounded.
A figure has one decimal place at most.
A figure reaching ten is written whole.
A figure that is a whole number is written without a decimal place.
A figure that floors onto zero is written as zero rather than as a signed zero.
A reading that is no finite number is written as the number that reading is.
Nothing here names a readout.
Nothing here reaches the store.
Nothing here decides a reading is too old to show.

definition: the rung a reading reaches on the scale it is read against
